tracks.text: The earth spins
A middle aged couple face each other, the man holding his wife's shoulders. The woman stares as cracks form across the man's face. Flesh splits, revealing rows of teeth and eyes.

She gasps as tendrils of flesh fan out like petals, with a circle of teeth and tentacles of eyes at the center. They expand out then close around her head, severing her neck. Blood splatters in all directions.
Lyrics, Let Me Hear, by Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas, originally in English and Japanese
You guys do not notice that we are gifted just by being humans
We are absolute predators
We do not even have any enemies
Maybe there are other animals watching us and thinking that "Someday we will beat them down"
Oh, we have the brains to think hard
Wear our favorite clothes
We are at no doubt human beings, many small lives
They were born with the fate of dying for someone
A human baby
When will they find out
That at the point they were born
We are the winners of the Earth?
Ah, I cried alone
Next to me, you asked a question
And so we nestle close together and live
until we sparkle
For what have I been living for?
When will I find the answer?
An answer that is only for you
What will myself and the...?!
Text, Stage 1, Metamorphosis
In the morning, a teenage boy with short brown hair sleeps alone in bed.
The boy shoots up and grabs his glasses, looking aroun
His computer and TV are turned off.
He blinks, and straightens his glasses
A man sits at a table, reading from a tablet. A woman stands in the kitchen. The boy, wearing a school uniform, approaches the table.
He sits in front of a plate of toast.
His mom hands him a plate with bacon and eggs.
His dad pokes his forehead as he takes a sip of tea. He notices a spider on the table and jumps.
Elsewhere, a middle aged man watches a news broadcast. The man wears a melted version of the newscaster's face.
The man's face changes back. He stumbles towards the door, leaving a trail of bloody footprints away from his wife's bloody, mangled corpse.
Students walk down suburban streets carrying book bags.
The boy walks slowly down the sidewalk. He wears a coat. Another student, wearing a scarf, passes him. A girl with chin length hair turns a corner and sees him.
She runs up behind him. She lifts a hand to chop his shoulder. His arm whips up and catches hers.
He blinks and turns around, finding her hand in his. She stares.
She stares at him wide eyed.
He stares, then slowly lowers his eyes down to his right hand, which is firmly grasping Murano's breast.
She slaps his face
Yuko picks up his glasses and offers them.
He puts on his glasses and looks at his hand.
He shoves it in his pocket
In class, Shinichi nods off
The teacher writes on the blackboard. Yuko, who sits next to him, glances over to see him tapping on his phone under the desk.

His eyes close. In a flashback, he sleeps in bed at night, listening to an MP3 player with earbuds. A worm crawls across his pillow. It has a drill shaped beak and dozens of tentacles stretching around its head. The worm approaches his ear and looks at his earbud.
The worm crawls up Shinichi's face, glows, and dives into his nostril.
He sits up and coughs the worm out, launching it across his bed. Shinichi blinks, then scrambles out of bed. He grabs a book and rolls it into a bat. He looks back at his empty bed.
The worm sits on his keyboard.
It launches toward him. He blocks with his right arm. The worm digs into his wrist.
The worm glows as it crawls up his arm, beneath the skin.
He wraps his earbud cords around his bicep as his parents come down the hallway
No hole
Yuko points to the teacher, standing over him
Later, Shinichi stands at a window, looking at his right hand. He looks up.
Shinichi walks down a suburban street. His head down, he approaches a crosswalk.
He backs away from the speeding car. He notices a ball bouncing into the street, and the young girl chasing after it.

The car stops abruptly, and its lights go out. Shinichi crouches down, shielding the girl, holding back the car. The hood has crumpled against his right hand, which has large claws and a single eyeball. Shinichi and the eyeball stare at each other, and his hand morphs back to normal.
The girl's mom runs and embraces her. Shinichi steps back, looks at his hand, clenches his fist, and runs away.
At the house, his mom reads a tabloid while drinking tea. She looks up towards the front door.
Shinichi closes the door to his room, panting. He throws his backpack on the bed, rifles through his desk drawer, and pulls out a knife.
He holds the knife high, shaking.

A slit forms between his index and middle finger. He balks. The slit forms lips and teeth, and the mouth moves to the center of the hand. His middle and ring fingers gain eyes at the tips and flail around. His index and pinky finger gain tiny, fingers, like baby hands.
Shinichi stabs. The hand monster catches the knife, breaks off the tip, and throws it back past his head into the ceiling.
He closes the window curtains
It turns lumpy
His hand returns to normal
He looks at his normal hand. He sits down, turns on his computer, launches BinGo!, and searches talking right hand. He skims the results and frowns.
Searches talking right hand strange snake.
He continues to frown. Outside, the sun sets. He searches alien invasion, then human takeover. He holds his head in his hands.
He bites into a second plate of curry
A drunk salary man stumbles through an alley
He steps in a pool of blood
A woman runs down a suburban street in the rain. She glances over to her neighbor, where dark strips hang from a clothes line
The strips are bloody flesh
Shinichi sits in his room, staring at his hand
He flicks his hand
He frowns
The morning
He rolls over
He straightens his glasses
His hand monster reads through textbooks
His arm has split in 2. Main monster flips pages, while the second one flaps wings. The main one flips more pages, and the second one turns into a fish.
The monster joins into one form, walks to the desk, grows arms to reach up to the computer, and pulls itself up, and starts typing.
split in half
He shakes his hand monster
He clenches his fist, then looks around at the textbooks scattered across the room
Shinichi eats toast at the dinner table. His father scrolls on a tablet while eating meat.
Father sighs, glances at the table, then grins
a spider
Shinichi picks it up, walks to the door, and releases it outside. His parents watch.
Shinichi walks down a suburban street. He pauses at an intersection.
He turns
A salaryman passes by
Shinichi pauses, grimacing. His hand monster stretches and pokes an eyeball around a corner, then looks back at him.
A side street with a small alley
He tries to run, but his hand monster grows and wraps around a telephone pole. He struggles to move. A mouth and eye grows out of his elbow and stare at him.
They approach the alley
A corgi wearing a sweater eats the insides of a dismembered mutt.
The corgi turns, its snout spread into several strips of flesh lined with teeth.
The dog monster, covered in blood, walks slowly towards him.
In the alley, the monster corgi splits its head in half. The halves grow longer and stretch wider. Shinichi sprints through streets, then ducks into a neighborhood park.
The eyeball tentacle nods. The monster corgi's stretches out its wide flaps, forming wings of stretched flesh. It takes flight.
The hand monster grows a long tentacle, reaching towards the wing headed corgi.
It stabs, and the corgi dodges. Stab, dodge, stab lands. The corgi's neck spits blood as the hand tentacle monster retreats, holding a heart. The corgi falls to the ground and shrivels.
The hand crushes the heart. Shinichi flinches. The monstrous corgi collapses, oozing blood.
Shinich stares at the hand monster, dripping with blood
He washes the hand at a faucet in the park.
A cityscape at night. Text, 2 days earlier.
In an alley, a man holds a knife, straddling a woman with torn clothes.
He licks his lips and stabs the woman in the heart. Her arms tense, then collapses. He licks the blood off his face. Above him, a light glistens in the sky.
A mote of light drifts slowly down. A green, almost fuzzy ball, resembling a textbook diagram of a virus.
It lands on a satellite and cracks in half. The glowing, drill beaked worm pokes its head out and looks around. It stares through a window at Shinichi, sleeping in bed.
Lyrics, It's the Right Time, by Daichi Miura, originally in Japanese
One day, those words you told me
Will become the unflinching resolve to head toward a wide ocean
In a small voice, with a sharpless answer and uncertain day
You murmur oh so silently
in a voice that you and I can hear
and it's the right time
Let's start walking
Yeah, it's the right time
Don't be afraid
Come on
To the place beyond that hill
Together, no matter how far
